setup: Bench behind you at about knee height
Top of your back foot on the bench
Front foot far enough out to drop straight down
execution: Drop your back knee toward the floor
Front knee follows your front toes
Lower until your front thigh is about level
Drive through your front foot to stand
faults: Pushing up mainly with the back leg
Front foot too close to the bench

notes: Use a stable bench that won't slide. Find your stance with bodyweight before adding dumbbells.
Choose a load you can balance. If you wobble or lean far forward, go lighter.
Finish all reps on one leg, then switch. Each side is logged separately and the load is each dumbbell.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view, figure facing right, bench behind the figure on the left, camera at hip height. Front leg is the near leg; rear leg is far, drawn behind.

keyPositions.label: Start
keyPositions.describe: Tall split stance. Front foot flat, front knee softly bent. Top of the rear foot (laces down) on a knee-height bench behind. Torso upright with a slight forward lean. Arms straight, dumbbells hanging at the sides.

keyPositions.label: Halfway
keyPositions.describe: Both knees bending, hips travelling mostly straight down. Front heel down, front knee over the toes. Dumbbells still hanging vertically.

keyPositions.label: Bottom
keyPositions.describe: Front thigh about level with the floor, front knee about 90°. Front shin angled slightly forward with the heel flat. Rear knee a few centimetres above the floor, rear thigh near vertical. Torso leaning forward about 15–25° with a neutral spine. Dumbbells vertical beside the front foot.

ikHints: Rear foot: top of the foot fixed on the bench edge in every frame
Rear knee at Bottom: a few centimetres above the floor, roughly below the hip
Front foot planted flat; hands fixed to the dumbbell handles
guideBrief.barPath: Dumbbells and hips move mostly straight down and up; small forward drift allowed, ≤ 4% of body height
emphasise: Front knee tracks over the toes
Rear foot stays on the bench while the rear knee drops toward the floor

sources.title: Mackey ER, Riemann BL (2021) Biomechanical differences between the Bulgarian split-squat and back squat. Int J Exerc Sci 14(1):533-543

Rear-leg angles are given as IK targets rather than numbers because they depend on bench height and leg length.
